## Proof

**Setup.** A "100 decimal digit number" is an integer $n$ with $10^{99} \le n \le 10^{100}-1$. The total count of such numbers is

$$T = (10^{100}-1) - 10^{99} + 1 = 10^{100} - 10^{99} = 9\cdot 10^{99}.$$

**Prime count via the Prime Number Theorem.** Let $\pi(x)$ denote the number of primes $\le x$. The PNT gives $\pi(x) \sim x/\ln x$, and more precisely the density of primes near a large value $t$ is $\approx 1/\ln t$. Hence the number of primes in $[10^{99},\,10^{100})$ is

$$P \;=\; \pi(10^{100})-\pi(10^{99}) \;\approx\; \int_{10^{99}}^{10^{100}} \frac{dt}{\ln t}.$$

Since $\ln t$ varies only by about $1\%$ across this interval (from $99\ln 10$ to $100\ln 10$), we may pull $1/\ln t$ out at the geometric-mean point $t = 10^{99.5}$ with negligible error:

$$P \;\approx\; \frac{10^{100}-10^{99}}{\ln(10^{99.5})} \;=\; \frac{9\cdot 10^{99}}{99.5\,\ln 10}.$$

**Percentage.**

$$\text{percentage} \;=\; \frac{P}{T}\times 100\% \;\approx\; \frac{1}{\ln(10^{99.5})}\times 100\% \;=\; \frac{100}{99.5\,\ln 10}\%.$$

Using $\ln 10 \approx 2.302585$ and $99.5\,\ln 10 \approx 229.107$:

$$\text{percentage} \;\approx\; \frac{100}{229.107}\% \;\approx\; 0.4365\%.$$

**Cross-check with the cruder PNT estimate.** Using $\pi(x)\approx x/\ln x$ directly:

$$P \approx \frac{10^{100}}{100\ln 10} - \frac{10^{99}}{99\ln 10} = \frac{10^{99}}{\ln 10}\Bigl(\tfrac{1}{10}-\tfrac{1}{99}\Bigr) = \frac{10^{99}}{\ln 10}\cdot\frac{89}{990},$$

$$\text{percentage} = \frac{P}{9\cdot 10^{99}}\times 100\% = \frac{8900}{8910\,\ln 10}\% = \frac{890}{891\,\ln 10}\% \approx \frac{890}{2051.6}\% \approx 0.4338\%.$$

The two estimates ($0.4365\%$ and $0.4338\%$) differ by less than $0.7\%$, consistent with the $\sim 1/\ln x$ relative error of the basic PNT. The logarithmic-integral (geometric-mean) value is the more accurate one.

**Result.** The percentage of prime numbers among all 100-digit numbers is, by the Prime Number Theorem, approximately

$$\boxed{\dfrac{100}{99.5\,\ln 10}\% \;\approx\; 0.436\%}.$$

Equivalently, roughly one in every $229$ hundred-digit numbers is prime.
